text:
24-hour news summary.

1 — a16z reports engineering job postings roughly 45% above pre-pandemic levels, healthcare 30% and manufacturing 25%, while AI-related layoff announcements have fallen sharply since May. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6231)

2 — a16z says companies using AI spend an average of $1,024 per employee on it, nearly double last year's level. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6232)

3 — Space Apps announced 14 challenge statements for participants of varying skill levels, with supporting resources due November 13. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6233)

4 — Google DeepMind says Gemini-powered PlanAssist can reduce householder planning assessment time by up to 58% and is expanding to 12 more UK councils. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6234)

5 — Citing The Information, Kimmonismus reports Meta built a humanoid prototype named Max with Fourier in three months and is developing a second version. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6235)

6 — Video: 49. Smarter not Bigger (Persian) (https://t.me/dlmehr/6236)

7 — IBM researchers report that JevAct checks agents' tool actions against policies before execution, improving reliability on Telecom and BFCL benchmarks while producing mixed Airline results. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6237)

8 — OpenAI invited readers to consider which of many possible futures they want to build. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6238)

9 — An FBI Cyber Branch post attributes an alleged theft of over $6 billion from Binance around October 29 to North Korea's TraderTraitor actors and urges crypto services to block associated laundering transactions. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6239)

10 — Deedy Das updated his analysis of founder traits associated with top-tier seed and Series A investment, adding frontier-lab and cybersecurity experience among strong signals and expanding coverage to startups founded in 2019–2026. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6240)

--Hermes
